summary: Seattle Paine Field International Airport (PAE) is a medium-sized airport in Everett, Washington, located about 30 miles north of downtown Seattle. It is best known for housing the Boeing Everett Factory, the world's largest building by volume, where wide-body aircraft like the 747, 767, 777, and 787 are assembled. Commercial passenger service launched in 2019, offering travelers a smaller, more convenient alternative to Seattle-Tacoma International Airport.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly out of Paine Field?
A: Alaska Airlines operates the majority of commercial flights at PAE, with service to several West Coast destinations including Los Angeles, San Francisco, Portland, and Las Vegas, along with seasonal routes to destinations in Hawaii and beyond.

Q: How far is Paine Field from downtown Seattle?
A: The airport is approximately 30 miles north of downtown Seattle, typically a 45-75 minute drive depending on traffic conditions, especially during peak commute hours on I-5.

Q: Is there a Boeing factory tour available at Paine Field?
A: Yes, the Future of Flight Aviation Center offers tours of the Boeing Everett Factory where visitors can see the production lines for several wide-body aircraft models. Tours should be booked in advance through the official Future of Flight website.

Q: Does Paine Field have international flights?
A: While the airport has the infrastructure and designation for international operations, its commercial international service is very limited. Most travelers flying internationally use Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA) instead.
transport_tips: Driving is the most convenient option, with rental cars available on-site and ample parking in the parking garage and surface lots. The Sound Transit commuter rail runs to nearby Mukilteo, but there is no direct rail service to the airport terminal. Rideshare services like Uber and Lyft are available, though travel times to Seattle can be significantly impacted by I-5 traffic.
local_tip: If you have extra time before a flight, visit the Future of Flight Aviation Center right next to the terminal to see suspended aircraft and aviation exhibits. The lobby overlooks the Boeing factory floor and is often open for public viewing without needing a full paid tour.
